quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Look to the sides, ahead, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides, ahead, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: A good driver watches all around their vehicle. You need to know what is happening beside, ahead, and behind your car at all times.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive if medication affects your driving ability?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive under the influence of any substance that affects your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep your speed the same.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed the same.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not speed up or brake. Keep your speed constant so the other vehicle can safely pass and merge back into your lane.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
Go before oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Never let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when turning left. Wait until the intersection is clear and traffic signals allow before you turn.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, drivers must:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to drivers.
Construction workers must yield to drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. Drivers must stop for pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks when traffic signals are not present.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also want to turn right, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn before the truck or bus does.
Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning first.
Try to squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning first.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: If you are very angry after an argument, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly while driving to distract yourself.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to reduce your anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your ability to drive safely. If you are angry, upset, worried, or scared, calm down before driving. You need to focus fully on the road.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Stop driving and rest if you feel tired. Tiredness slows your reactions and dulls your thinking, which makes driving dangerous.

questions.question: If a pedestrian is crossing your lane without a crosswalk, you should:

options.text: Make sure they see you before moving forward.
Drive carefully around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross the road first, even without a marked crosswalk. Drivers must always give pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What is this symbol used for?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle shows it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks like a solid orange triangle during the day and a hollow red triangle at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here would be unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area for road construction workers.
An area where pedestrians can cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area where pedestrians can cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked with white lines to show where people can cross. They may have extra lines between or instead of the parallel lines. Some crosswalks have no markings.

questions.question: When driving on a narrow, winding road, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Keep your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You should slow down in difficult driving conditions. Speed limits are only for ideal conditions.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness and concentration, increases reaction time, and reduces coordination.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Night driving is challenging because:

options.text: Speed limits are higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is difficult because low visibility makes it hard to judge distance and how fast other vehicles are traveling. You can only see as far as your headlights allow.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Honk to let them know to move.
Yield the right-of-way.
Swerve around them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you see a blind person crossing a street at a crosswalk or intersection, be careful and show courtesy. Let them cross safely before you go.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer to the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Do not panic if you have a blowout. Hold the wheel firmly and take your foot off the accelerator to let the car slow down. Apply the brakes lightly when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed significantly.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn you of a school zone or school crossing. When you see these signs, stay alert and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Stay alert and follow their instructions.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross into the other lane. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden, improper lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden, improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for drivers making sudden, improper lane changes. Do not challenge them. Stay away from aggressive drivers.

questions.question: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol harm judgment and coordination. Any amount of alcohol can impair your driving ability.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow traffic laws and always signal your lane changes.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones protect workers and drivers. Watch for cones, signs, and workers in bright vests.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car) can:

options.text: Frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Never result in a traffic ticket.
Prevent being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating causes anger and aggressive driving. Avoid it or you may face legal consequences.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is beginning.
The road will be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is beginning.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is starting ahead. Stay to the right of the median.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
It is not safe to pass.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: "No passing zone" signs mean you cannot pass. These areas have poor visibility and are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings with warning signs or flashing lights. Do not drive around lowered gates. It is illegal.
